sections.content:
You know *acabar de* + infinitive from A2 Unit 32: *Acabo de llegar* ("I have just arrived") and *Acababa de salir cuando me llamaste*. This lesson adds what the tense does.

With the present, *acaba de* means "has just": *Acaba de llegar*. With the imperfect, *acababa de* means "had just" and sets the scene before something else happens, which is how stories use it: *Acababa de salir cuando empezó a llover*. In the preterite the meaning changes: *Acabó de comer* means "He finished eating", not "he has just eaten".

sections.title: acabar de + infinitive
rows: Acabo de hablar con el capataz.
I have just spoken to the foreman.
Acababa de salir cuando empezó a llover.
I had just left when it started to rain.
Acabó de ensillar el caballo y salió.
He finished saddling the horse and left.

sections.content: *Acabar de* means "just" only in the present and the imperfect. With a time far in the past, use the preterite of the main verb: not *acaba de llegar hace cinco años*, but *llegó hace cinco años*.
